scope: Offline bounded research and extractive summarization from user-supplied documents; built from an empty directory.

request_schema.question: nonempty string
request_schema.documents: list of objects containing exactly id and text; both nonempty strings; IDs unique

interface.citation_offsets: Zero-based, half-open Python Unicode character offsets in original document text, not UTF-8 bytes.
interface.callback_contract: Receives a deep copy of retrieval output. Returns exactly {findings: [{text, citations}]}. Citations must name known source IDs, contain exact source spans, and lie within selected evidence. Text must equal citation quotes joined with single spaces. Unsupported paraphrases are rejected.
interface.cli_errors: Malformed input emits a JSON error to stderr and exits 2; successful output is JSON on stdout and exit 0.

implementation: Unicode case-folded word tokenization with a fixed English stopword set.
Sentence-like source segmentation and 600-character chunks with 100-character overlap for long spans.
BM25 term-frequency, inverse-document-frequency and length-normalized ranking, multiplied by query-term coverage.
Stable source-order tie breaking; exact extractive findings with independently verifiable citation spans.
Case-folded whitespace-normalized duplicate merging retains all exact source citations.
Any same-source overlap with selected evidence is suppressed.
Separately reports terms absent from all passages and terms excluded by selection.
Reports potential numeric or polarity conflicts among lexically similar selected findings without deciding which source is correct.
Optional callback output is strictly validated without using any external model or provider.
limitations: Lexical retrieval has no embeddings, stemming, synonym expansion, source credibility evaluation, external search or factual verification.
A lexical match can be tangential; complete term coverage is not evidence that a question has been answered.
Missing evidence describes lexical gaps in the supplied sources only, not absence of real-world evidence.
Sentence splitting is heuristic and can split decimals or abbreviations; long chunks can split words. Citation offsets nevertheless remain exact.
Overlap suppression may omit distinct nearby content. The finite finding limit can exclude relevant evidence.
Conflict detection is a heuristic warning over selected findings only; it can miss semantic conflicts or flag differences explained by context, dates or entities.
Duplicate normalization can merge differently capitalized or spaced text; each retained citation preserves its own original exact quotation.
Duplicate citation counts are bounded indirectly by source character limits, not by a separate per-finding provenance cap.
The optional callback supports grounded quote selection and concatenation, not free-form paraphrasing or semantic entailment verification.
The module cannot sandbox or time-limit arbitrary caller-provided callback code. No callback contacting a provider was used.
Measurements are local functional test outcomes, not benchmark quality, usage, cost or client-score estimates.

coverage: Labeled relevance, Unicode span and query-coverage fixtures
Malformed documents and requests, duplicate IDs and resource bounds
No match, empty source collection, stopword-only question and partial evidence
Duplicate provenance and overlapping long-passage suppression
Labeled numeric and polarity conflicts; nonconflicting documents
Finding cap, uncovered query terms, deterministic output and input immutability
Valid injected callback and rejection of unknown IDs, false quotes, invalid offsets, unsupported text and unretrieved evidence
CLI example success and malformed-JSON error exit

execution_constraints.usage_accounting: Actual agent build-token collection is owned by the parent; this manifest does not estimate usage, costs or client scores.
